sources.entry: OpenReplay | Session replay and product analytics

summary.one_liner: OpenReplay is a self-hosted, open-source experience platform offering session replay, DevTools-style debugging, product analytics, and live cobrowsing.
summary.what_it_does: OpenReplay records user sessions so teams can replay what users clicked, navigated, and hit, with console logs, network activity, JS errors, store state, and 40+ performance metrics attached. Product analytics covers funnels, trends, journeys, heatmaps, and web analytics, each linked to underlying session replays. Cobrowsing lets support staff view a user's live screen, take cursor control with permission, and start a WebRTC call. Capture-time sanitization can mask CSS selectors, redact inputs, and sanitize network payloads, and a private mode masks all text and inputs by default. The README also lists a free Chrome extension called Spot for capturing bugs, native mobile replay for iOS, Android, and React Native, and SDKs for many web frameworks.
use_cases: self-host session replay for users' data privacy
debug frontend bugs with full browser context
watch user sessions to find UX friction
replay sessions for regulated industries like healthcare or banking
how_to_run: Start with the Getting Started guide in the OpenReplay documentation
Deploy on a single VM with at least 2 vCPUs, 8 GB RAM, and 50 GB storage
Deployment options listed: Docker, Kubernetes (Helm), Ubuntu bare metal, or from source
Install the JavaScript tracker SDK in your web app (framework guides or drop-in snippet)
stack: iOS, Android, and React Native SDKs
notable: Self-hosted so session data stays in the user's own infrastructure, with first-party tracking that ad blockers do not block
Capture-time sanitization and private mode mask data before it reaches the server
Combines session replay, DevTools, product analytics, and cobrowsing in one platform
Integrates with Redux, Vuex, Pinia, MobX, NgRx, Zustand, plus Sentry, Datadog, Jira, and Slack
caveats: Self-hosting requires a VM baseline of 2 vCPUs, 8 GB RAM, and 50 GB storage; the README describes this as a minimum baseline
Mobile SDKs are currently in beta
Monorepo uses multiple licenses; the ee/ directory (Enterprise Edition) uses a separate commercial license
summary.license: AGPLv3 for most of the codebase; some directories MIT; ee/ directory under a separate commercial license
